aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abdi-2.title: Abdi
abdi-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
abdi-2.note: Another man of the name from the same stretch of years. He appears in one verse, in a Levitical list, and nothing else is said about him.

abdon.title: Abdon
abdon.note: A Levitical town in Asher's territory, also written Ebron. It shows up in the allotment lists and barely anywhere else.

abel-maim.title: Abel-maim
abel-maim.note: Another name for Abel-beth-maachah, meaning Abel on the waters, and the form used when Asa hires Ben-hadad to attack Israel's northern towns. Assyria took the city about a century later, and Tiglath-pileser's own account of that campaign names it.

abi.title: Abi
abi.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
abi.note: One of 8 men called Abi. This one is a woman from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

abiah.title: Abiah
abiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
abiah.note: A name shared by kings, priests and Levites, which is why it covers so much ground. The one who gets the most space is Rehoboam's son, who ruled Judah for a short time and beat Jeroboam's army while badly outnumbered.

abihail-4.title: Abihail
abihail-4.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
abihail-4.note: A wife of Rehoboam. She appears in a single verse.

abishalom.title: Abishalom
abishalom.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
abishalom.note: This is Absalom, David's third son. He killed his half-brother Amnon for raping their sister Tamar, and when David punished neither of them he spent years quietly building support before taking the throne by force. The revolt ended with his famous hair caught in an oak while he was still riding.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

adaiah-3.title: Adaiah
adaiah-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
adaiah-3.note: A man of the name from the divided-kingdom years, whom Chronicles names once.

adnah.title: Adnah
adnah.note: Jehoshaphat's senior commander, at the head of 300,000 men, the largest single division named when the king reorganised his army.

adonijah-2.title: Adonijah
adonijah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
adonijah-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

adoraim.title: Adoraim
adoraim.note: Rehoboam fortified it after the kingdom split, one link in Judah's southern line of defence. The name survives in Dura, a village southwest of Hebron.

adoram-2.title: Adoram
adoram-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
adoram-2.note: One of 3 men called Adoram. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Chronicles.

adullam.title: Adullam
adullam.note: A Canaanite royal city in the Shephelah, near the valley of Elah. David killed Goliath in that valley. Later, running from Saul, he hid in a cave near Adullam, and his family joined him there, and so did everyone in distress.

ahab.title: Ahab
ahab.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahab.note: King of northern Israel for about twenty-two years. He married Jezebel, a Phoenician princess. She brought Baal worship into a kingdom that was supposed to belong to Yahweh alone, and he let her.

ahaz.title: Ahaz
ahaz.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahaz.note: He abandoned his predecessors' reforms, sacrificed his own son in the fire and closed the temple. Facing a coalition of enemies, he paid Assyria for protection instead of trusting the promise Isaiah brought, and Judah stayed an Assyrian vassal for a generation. The Immanuel prophecy was given in his crisis.

ahaziah.title: Ahaziah
ahaziah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahaziah.note: Ahab's grandson through his mother Athaliah, and king of Judah for only one year. He was killed in the same purge that brought Jehu to power.

ahaziah-2.title: Ahaziah
ahaziah-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahaziah-2.note: He ruled northern Israel, fell through a palace lattice, and sent to a foreign god to ask about healing. Elijah rebuked him for not asking the Lord.

ahiah.title: Ahiah
ahiah.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
ahiah.note: Ahijah, the prophet from Shiloh. He tore his own cloak into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam, for the ten tribes about to be torn from Solomon's line, and after Solomon died the kingdom split just that way.

ahikam.title: Ahikam
ahikam.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahikam.note: A court official under Josiah. He backed the warnings of Huldah the prophetess and later protected Jeremiah from a mob that wanted him killed, and Gedaliah was his son.

aijalon.title: Aijalon
aijalon.note: In the valley of Aijalon Joshua told the moon to stand still alongside the sun during the battle against the Amorite coalition. Later it marked the boundary of Danite and Benjamite territory.

amariah-5.title: Amariah
amariah-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amariah-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

amariah-6.title: Amariah
amariah-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amariah-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

amasa-2.title: Amasa
amasa-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amasa-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

amasai-4.title: Amasai
amasai-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amasai-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

amasiah.title: Amasiah
amasiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amasiah.note: In Jehoshaphat's army he commanded a thousand men, and he is remembered for volunteering himself for the LORD's service. Nothing further is recorded about him.

amaziah.title: Amaziah
amaziah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amaziah.note: He took Judah's throne after his father Joash was assassinated and executed the killers but spared their children, as the law said. Then he beat Edom, brought its idols home and worshipped them. A war he picked with northern Israel ended with him captured and Jerusalem's walls torn down.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amon.title: Amon
amon.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amon.note: The son of Manasseh. He followed his father's early idolatry and never turned back, and his own officials killed him after two years. The people executed the plotters and made his young son Josiah king.

amon-2.title: Amon
amon-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amon-2.note: 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

amoz.title: Amoz
amoz.about: Isaiah's father living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amoz.note: Isaiah's father, and not the prophet Amos: the names look alike in English but come from different Hebrew names entirely.

arabia.title: Arabia
arabia.note: Paul says he went away into Arabia for a time after his conversion, and in the New Testament the word covers the region south and east of Judea.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

asa.title: Asa
asa.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asa.note: King of Judah for forty-one years, and a real reformer. He removed his own grandmother as queen mother over an obscene idol and drove the male shrine prostitutes out. Early on he trusted God against a huge Cushite invasion, but late in life he hired a foreign king against northern Israel instead.

asahel-2.title: Asahel
asahel-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asahel-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

asahel-3.title: Asahel
asahel-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asahel-3.note: One of 4 men called Asahel. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

asaiah.title: Asaiah
asaiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asaiah.note: One of the officials Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah.

asaph.title: Asaph
asaph.about: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asaph.note: A Levite David put in charge of one of the temple choirs. Twelve psalms carry his name, Psalm 50 and Psalms 73 to 83, which means either he wrote them or a guild of musicians kept his name for generations.

ashdod.title: Ashdod
ashdod.note: Ashdod spelled another way, one of the five chief Philistine cities, on the coast between Ekron and Gaza. The captured ark was put in its temple of Dagon, and the affliction started there.

asher.title: Asher
asher.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asher.note: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.

asshur.title: Asshur
asshur.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
asshur.note: Shem's son, whose name stuck to the land and empire of Assyria on the upper Tigris. Assyria became the great power of the eighth and seventh centuries BC, deported Israel's northern tribes after Samaria fell, and kept threatening Judah.

athaliah.title: Athaliah
athaliah.about: Queen living at the time of Divided Monarchy
athaliah.note: Ahab and Jezebel's daughter, married into Judah's royal house. When her son Ahaziah was killed she took the throne and murdered nearly the whole royal family, the only woman to rule Judah in her own name. Six years later the priest Jehoiada brought out the infant Joash, who had survived, and she was executed.

attai-3.title: Attai
attai-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
attai-3.note: One of 3 men called Attai. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

azaliah.title: Azaliah
azaliah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azaliah.note: Shaphan's father. Shaphan was the royal scribe who read the newly found Book of the Law to King Josiah.

azariah-13.title: Azariah
azariah-13.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah-13.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

azariah-14.title: Azariah
azariah-14.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah-14.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

azariah-15.title: Azariah
azariah-15.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah-15.note: One of 17 men called Azariah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

azariah-16.title: Azariah
azariah-16.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah-16.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him. The verse is 2 Chronicles 29:12.

azariah-8.title: Azariah
azariah-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him. The verses are 2 Chronicles 31:10 and 2 Chronicles 31:13.

azariah.title: Azariah
azariah.about: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah.note: This is King Uzziah of Judah under his other name.

azariah-7.title: Azariah
azariah-7.about: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah-7.note: One of 17 men called Azariah. This one is a priest from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in 2 Chronicles.

azariah-12.title: Azariah
azariah-12.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah-12.note: A prophet from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

azaziah-3.title: Azaziah
azaziah-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azaziah-3.note: A Levitical name. One Azaziah was a musician under David; this one is an overseer in the temple stores.

azekah.title: Azekah
azekah.note: A fortified town in Judah's Shephelah. Joshua routed five Amorite kings near it in a hailstorm. A Lachish ostracon written during Nebuchadnezzar's last campaign says the writer is watching for Lachish's signal fires but cannot see Azekah, which some read as Azekah already fallen and others as a line of sight he never had.

azrikam-4.title: Azrikam
azrikam-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azrikam-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

azubah-2.title: Azubah
azubah-2.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azubah-2.note: Jehoshaphat's mother. Kings and Chronicles both name her in the notice of his reign and give her nothing more.

baal.title: Baal
baal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal.note: The Canaanite storm god, the power people believed sent the rain and made the crops grow. Worshipping him was the temptation Israel never shook, and the Old Testament fights it from the judges onward.

baalath.title: Baalath
baalath.note: Dan was given this town, and Solomon later fortified it as one of his store cities. The name means mistress or lady.

baasha.title: Baasha
baasha.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
baasha.note: He killed Nadab, Israel's second king, and wiped out the rest of Jeroboam's family to take the northern throne. That fulfilled a prophecy against Jeroboam's line. Baasha's own violence brought the same kind of end on his house.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

ben-hail.title: Ben-hail
ben-hail.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ben-hail.note: King Jehoshaphat sent him out, with priests and Levites, to teach the Book of the Law in the towns of Judah.

benaiah-7.title: Benaiah
benaiah-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
benaiah-7.note: One of 12 men called Benaiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

benaiah-8.title: Benaiah
benaiah-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
benaiah-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

benhadad.title: Benhadad
benhadad.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
benhadad.note: The name was a royal title in Aram-Damascus, carried by at least two kings and possibly three, all of them at war with Israel. This one is the Ben-hadad of 1 Kings 15 and 20.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

berachah-2.title: Berachah
berachah-2.note: The valley where Jehoshaphat's army blessed God after the battle, which is how it got the name.

berachiah-6.title: Berachiah
berachiah-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
berachiah-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

beth-horon.title: Beth-horon
beth-horon.note: Twin towns on the pass from the coastal plain up into the hill country. Joshua's army came this way chasing the Canaanite coalition in the battle where the sun stood still.

beth-shemesh.title: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh.note: It was a Levitical city on Judah's northern border, its name meaning house of the sun. When the Philistines sent the ark back, it came here first and was welcomed with sacrifice.

beth-zur.title: Beth-zur
beth-zur.note: A fortified town in the hill country of Judah, a few miles north of Hebron. Rehoboam strengthened it as part of the defences of his kingdom once the ten northern tribes had broken away.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bezaleel.title: Bezaleel
bezaleel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
bezaleel.note: God named him and filled him with his Spirit to design and build the tabernacle and everything in it, the ark of the covenant included. He is the first person in the Bible described as filled with the Spirit.

boaz-2.title: Boaz
boaz-2.note: Named twice, in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

carchemish.title: Carchemish
carchemish.note: A major city on the west bank of the Euphrates. For a long time it was a Hittite provincial capital, and later the seat of a Neo-Hittite kingdom of its own. Nebuchadnezzar crushed Pharaoh Necho's army there.

chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

chenaanah.title: Chenaanah
chenaanah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
chenaanah.note: His son Zedekiah was a false prophet who promised King Ahab victory and struck the true prophet Micaiah in the face for saying otherwise.

conaniah.title: Conaniah
conaniah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
conaniah.note: A Levite in charge of the tithes and offerings that came into the temple under Hezekiah's reforms.

cyrus.title: Cyrus
cyrus.about: Emperor living at the time of Exile and Return
cyrus.note: The Persian king who took Babylon and let the deported peoples, the Jews among them, go home and rebuild their temples. Isaiah calls him by name long before he was born, God's shepherd and anointed. The Cyrus Cylinder, found in Babylon in 1879, records the same policy.

damascus.title: Damascus
damascus.note: A city has stood here, on a fertile plain watered by the Barada northwest of Mount Hermon, since before the patriarchs. It was the Aramean capital that fought Israel through the ninth and eighth centuries BC. Saul was converted on the road into it, and the street called Straight was a real colonnaded street whose columns have been found.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

dodavah.title: Dodavah
dodavah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
dodavah.note: A man of Mareshah. His son Eliezer rebuked Jehoshaphat for joining Ahaziah of Israel in a shipbuilding venture, and God destroyed the ships.

eden-3.title: Eden
eden-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eden-3.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

eden-4.title: Eden
eden-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eden-4.note: One of 3 men called Eden. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

edomite.title: Edomite
edomite.note: Esau's descendants, living in Seir south and east of the Dead Sea. Kin to Israel and at odds with it for most of the record. Egyptian texts mention Edom as early as the thirteenth century BC, and its capital Busayra and the copper works at Khirbat en Nahas have both been excavated.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

elath.title: Elath
elath.note: A port on the Gulf of Aqaba near Ezion-geber. Solomon held it, Edom took it back, Uzziah recovered it for Judah, and Syria finally got it. Modern Eilat keeps the name.

eliab-2.title: Eliab
eliab-2.about: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
eliab-2.note: David's eldest brother. He was tall and looked the part, and Samuel thought he was the one until God told him the Lord looks at the heart. Later he tore into David for turning up at the Goliath battle line.

eliada-3.title: Eliada
eliada-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliada-3.note: One of 3 men called Eliada. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

eliakim.title: Eliakim
eliakim.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliakim.note: Hezekiah's palace administrator, sent with the other officials to talk to the Rabshakeh while Sennacherib had Jerusalem under siege. Another Eliakim was the king Necho renamed Jehoiakim.

eliel-8.title: Eliel
eliel-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliel-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

eliezer-5.title: Eliezer
eliezer-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliezer-5.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

elijah.title: Elijah
elijah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elijah.note: A prophet from Tishbe in Gilead who took on Ahab and Jezebel over Baal worship and beat 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel with fire from heaven. Straight after, he ran into the wilderness sure he was the last faithful man left, and God met him in a quiet voice, not in wind or earthquake or fire. He did not die; a whirlwind took him up while Elisha watched.

elishama-6.title: Elishama
elishama-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elishama-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

elishaphat.title: Elishaphat
elishaphat.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elishaphat.note: One of the army commanders Jehoiada brought into the covenant to put the boy Joash on the throne. The coup ended Athaliah's six years, the only gap in the Davidic line on Judah's throne.

elizaphan.title: Elizaphan
elizaphan.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
elizaphan.note: He led the Kohathite Levites in the wilderness. When Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire, he was one of those who carried the bodies out.

elkanah-8.title: Elkanah
elkanah-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elkanah-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

en-gedi.title: En-gedi
en-gedi.note: An oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, fed by a spring that drops some 600 feet down the cliffs. David hid in its caves from Saul and spared Saul's life there. A Chalcolithic temple on the site is far older than Israel in Canaan.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

etam-3.title: Etam
etam-3.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

euphrates.title: Euphrates
euphrates.note: The great river. It rises in the Armenian highlands and runs some seventeen hundred miles to the Persian Gulf. Genesis has it as one of Eden's four rivers, the promise to Abraham reaches to it, and later Assyria and Babylon came from beyond it.

ezion-geber.title: Ezion-geber
ezion-geber.note: Solomon built his fleet here, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba near Elath, to sail for Ophir, and Jehoshaphat's ships were wrecked here later. Nelson Glueck dug Tell el-Kheleifeh in the 1930s and called it the site, though later work on the pottery has kept the question open.

gaba.title: Gaba
gaba.note: Another English spelling of Geba, a Levitical city in Benjamin by the pass of Michmash. Jonathan raided a Philistine garrison there, and later it marked the line between the northern and southern kingdoms.

gad-2.title: Gad
gad-2.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
gad-2.note: A prophet of the united monarchy, and nothing to do with Jacob's son. He first turns up in 1 Samuel 22:5, comes back in 2 Samuel 24, and Chronicles names him again.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gederoth.title: Gederoth
gederoth.note: The Philistines took it in the reign of Ahaz, while Judah was worn down by war with Israel and Syria. It was a Shephelah town, and the name means sheepfolds.

gerar.title: Gerar
gerar.note: Abraham and Isaac both stayed in this Philistine town in the Negev under a king called Abimelech, and both passed their wives off as sisters out of fear. Isaac reaped a hundredfold there and dug out his father's wells again until quarrels over water moved him on toward Beersheba. Tel Haror is a leading candidate for the site.

gibeon.title: Gibeon
gibeon.note: They tricked Joshua into a treaty by dressing as travellers from far away, the Hivites of this city northwest of Jerusalem, and so they lived but served at Israel's sanctuary. The tabernacle stood at Gibeon for years, and Solomon had his dream there. At el-Jib dozens of jar handles stamped with the name have settled where it was.

gihon.title: Gihon
gihon.note: Two waters carry the name. One is a river out of Eden that circles Cush and has never been matched to a known river. The other is Jerusalem's only natural spring, in the Kidron Valley, which Hezekiah ran underground into the city before Sennacherib's siege, and the tunnel can still be walked.

gimzo.title: Gimzo
gimzo.note: The Philistines took it and its villages in the reign of Ahaz. It was a lowland town known for sycamores, and the name survives in Jimzu, a village southeast of Lydda.

gur-baal.title: Gur-baal
gur-baal.note: God helped King Uzziah beat the people of Gur-baal, along with the Philistines and the Meunites. The name means sojourn of Baal, so it was probably an Arabian settlement where Baal was worshipped, and nobody knows where.

hadlai.title: Hadlai
hadlai.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hadlai.note: An Ephraimite, named only as father of Amasa, one of four Ephraimite chiefs who stood in front of the returning army and made them release and care for the Judean captives.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hamath-zobah.title: Hamath-Zobah
hamath-zobah.note: Solomon captured it and rebuilt it as a store city, and whether it is Hamath on the Orontes or a separate stronghold tied to Zobah is disputed.

hanani.title: Hanani
hanani.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hanani.note: The prophet who went to King Asa and told him he had leaned on a foreign alliance instead of on God.

hananiah-6.title: Hananiah
hananiah-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hananiah-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

hashabiah-7.title: Hashabiah
hashabiah-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hashabiah-7.note: One of 10 men called Hashabiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

hasrah.title: Hasrah
hasrah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hasrah.note: Huldah the prophetess was his wife, and Josiah's officials went to her when the Book of the Law was found. He kept the vestments, and Kings spells him Harhas.

hazael.title: Hazael
hazael.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hazael.note: Elijah was told to anoint him king of Aram, and the prophet wept over what Hazael would do to Israel. He smothered his own king to get the throne and was one of Israel's worst enemies for decades. An inscription with his name has been found in Damascus.

hazezon-tamar.title: Hazezon-tamar
hazezon-tamar.note: An Amorite town by the Dead Sea that Chedorlaomer's kings attacked in Abraham's day, later called En-gedi. The old name comes back in Jehoshaphat's reign, when Moabites, Ammonites and Meunites come up against Judah from there.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

heman.title: Heman
heman.about: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
heman.note: David put him among the chief musicians over the worship, a Levite. Psalm 88, one of the darkest laments in the book, is credited to him.

hezekiah.title: Hezekiah
hezekiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hezekiah.note: One of Judah's few good kings. He came after Ahaz, reopened the temple, tore down the high places, and broke up the bronze serpent Moses had made once people began worshipping it. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem in 701 BC, Hezekiah prayed, Isaiah promised deliverance, and the siege broke overnight. His seal impression has been dug up near the Temple Mount, and his tunnel still runs under the city.

hillkiah.title: Hillkiah
hillkiah.about: High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hillkiah.note: The high priest under Josiah who found a forgotten scroll of the law while the temple was being repaired. What he found set off Judah's last great reform.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

horeb.title: Horeb
horeb.note: Another name for Sinai, where Moses met God at the burning bush and Israel received the law, and where Elijah later ran and heard God in a still, small voice after the wind, earthquake and fire.

huldah.title: Huldah
huldah.about: Prophetess living at the time of Divided Monarchy
huldah.note: Josiah's officials took the scroll found in the temple to her, a prophetess in Jerusalem, and not to any of the men prophesying at the time. She told them it was genuine. Judgment was coming on Judah, she said, though not in Josiah's lifetime.

hur.title: Hur
hur.about: Aaron's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hur.note: He helped Aaron hold up Moses's arms while Israel fought Amalek, since Israel won as long as those hands stayed up. When Moses went up Sinai for the law, Hur was left in charge with Aaron.

huram.title: Huram
huram.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
huram.note: Chronicles spells the king of Tyre this way. He is the Hiram who sent materials for Solomon's temple.

huram-2.title: Huram
huram-2.about: Syrian living at the time of United Monarchy
huram-2.note: The bronzeworker the king of Tyre sent to make the temple's furnishings, spelled Huram in Chronicles and Hiram elsewhere.

iddo-2.title: Iddo
iddo-2.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
iddo-2.note: A seer whose writings Chronicles cites for the reigns of Solomon, Rehoboam and Abijah. The writings themselves are lost.

ijon.title: Ijon
ijon.note: In Naphtali, in Israel's far north. Ben-hadad took it at Asa's request, and later Tiglath-pileser III took it in Pekah's reign, a conquest his own inscriptions also list. It is usually identified with Tell Dibbin.

imla.title: Imla
imla.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
imla.note: Micaiah's father. Micaiah was the one prophet at Ahab's court who would contradict the four hundred and say Ahab would die in battle.

imna-3.title: Imna
imna-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
imna-3.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

isaiah.title: Isaiah
isaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
isaiah.note: Amoz's son, a prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century, who counselled four kings of Judah and is quoted in the New Testament more than any other prophet. He gave his two sons names that were sermons, Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he told Hezekiah the city would stand, and the Taylor Prism brags of the siege without ever claiming the city fell.

ishmael-4.title: Ishmael
ishmael-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ishmael-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

ishmael-5.title: Ishmael
ishmael-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ishmael-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

ismachiah.title: Ismachiah
ismachiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ismachiah.note: In Hezekiah's reforms the temple filled with tithes and gifts, and Ismachiah was one of the Levites set over them, with Cononiah and Shimei, under the high priest Azariah.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

jabneh.title: Jabneh
jabneh.note: Uzziah broke down Jabneh's walls after beating the Philistines. It is the same town as Jabneel, and as Jamnia, or Yavne, it became a centre of Jewish learning after the temple fell in 70 AD.

jachin-3.title: Jachin
jachin-3.note: Named twice, in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

jahath-4.title: Jahath
jahath-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jahath-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

jahaziel-4.title: Jahaziel
jahaziel-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jahaziel-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

japha.title: Japha
japha.note: The Hebrew name for Joppa, the port that is Jaffa today. Solomon's cedar came in by sea there, and so did Ezra's timber for the second temple, and Jonah sailed from it toward Tarshish. The Amarna letters already mention its guarded gate.

jecholiah.title: Jecholiah
jecholiah.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jecholiah.note: Amaziah's wife and Uzziah's mother, a woman of Jerusalem. Her son came to the throne at sixteen and reigned over fifty years. Nothing further is recorded of her.

jeduthun.title: Jeduthun
jeduthun.about: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
jeduthun.note: David put three chief musicians over temple worship, Heman, Asaph and Jeduthun. Several psalms carry Jeduthun's name in their headings.

jehalellel-2.title: Jehalellel
jehalellel-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehalellel-2.note: The name means praise God. This one is a Levite whose sons helped clean out the temple.

jehiel-5.title: Jehiel
jehiel-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehiel-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

jehiel-6.title: Jehiel
jehiel-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehiel-6.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

jehiel-7.title: Jehiel
jehiel-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehiel-7.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

jehiel.title: Jehiel
jehiel.about: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehiel.note: One of the temple musicians David appointed when the ark came up, playing before it. The name was common in Levitical families in Chronicles.

jehoaddan.title: Jehoaddan
jehoaddan.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoaddan.note: Jehoash's wife, and Amaziah's mother. She came from Jerusalem, and the record gives her the brief notice most queen mothers of Judah get.

jehoahaz.title: Jehoahaz
jehoahaz.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoahaz.note: King of northern Israel, and a weak one, worn down by Aramean pressure through his reign.

jehoahaz-2.title: Jehoahaz
jehoahaz-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoahaz-2.note: Josiah's son. He reigned in Judah three months before Pharaoh Necho deposed him and took him to Egypt, where he died.

jehohanan.title: Jehohanan
jehohanan.about: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehohanan.note: A gatekeeper at the temple under David. The name was common, and one man of it led troops under Jehoshaphat.

jehohanan-2.title: Jehohanan
jehohanan-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehohanan-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

jehohanan-3.title: Jehohanan
jehohanan-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehohanan-3.note: One of 8 men called Jehohanan. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

jehoiachin.title: Jehoiachin
jehoiachin.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiachin.note: Three months on Judah's throne, then he surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar and went to Babylon with much of Jerusalem's upper class. He spent thirty-seven years a prisoner. A new Babylonian king let him out and fed him at the royal table for the rest of his life, and 2 Kings ends there.

jehoiada.title: Jehoiada
jehoiada.about: High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiada.note: After Athaliah killed the royal family, this priest hid the baby Joash in the temple for six years and then led the coup that put him on the throne. While Jehoiada lived, Joash ruled well. They buried him among the kings.

jehoiakim.title: Jehoiakim
jehoiakim.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiakim.note: Pharaoh Necho put him on Judah's throne. When Jeremiah's scroll was read to him, he cut it off a section at a time and burned it in the fire pot, while his advisors begged him to stop. Jeremiah had it written out again, with more added.

jehoram.title: Jehoram
jehoram.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoram.note: Two kings had the name. One was Ahab's son in Israel, killed by Jehu; the other ruled Judah, killed his brothers, married Ahab's daughter Athaliah and brought Baal worship south, and died of the long illness Elijah had foretold.

jehoram-2.title: Jehoram
jehoram-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoram-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

jehoshabeath.title: Jehoshabeath
jehoshabeath.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoshabeath.note: King Jehoram's daughter and the priest Jehoiada's wife. When Athaliah set out to kill the royal family, she hid the baby Joash and his nurse in a temple storeroom, and Kings calls her Jehosheba.

jehoshaphat.title: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoshaphat.note: A king of Judah who sent officials and Levites through the land to teach the law. His alliance with Israel kept going wrong, and in one battle enemy soldiers took him for Ahab and nearly killed him. When Moab, Ammon and Edom invaded together, he sent singers ahead of the army, and the invaders destroyed each other.

jehozabad-3.title: Jehozabad
jehozabad-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehozabad-3.note: One of 3 men called Jehozabad. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

jehozabad.title: Jehozabad
jehozabad.about: Moabite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehozabad.note: One of the two servants who killed King Joash of Judah. Chronicles gives his mother as a Moabite woman.

jehu.title: Jehu
jehu.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehu.note: Anointed king by one of Elisha's students with a single job, to wipe out Ahab's family, and he did it thoroughly: Joram, Jezebel, every descendant left, then Baal's priests tricked into one building and killed together. The Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III shows an Israelite bowing and paying tribute, named as Jehu, though whether the figure is the king himself or his envoy is argued either way.

jehu-2.title: Jehu
jehu-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehu-2.note: A prophet, not the king of the same name. In Kings he speaks judgment against a king of Israel, and in Chronicles he rebukes a southern king and writes up that king's reign.

jehush-5.title: Jehush
jehush-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehush-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

jeiel-4.title: Jeiel
jeiel-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeiel-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

jeiel-5.title: Jeiel
jeiel-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeiel-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

jeiel-6.title: Jeiel
jeiel-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeiel-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

jeiel.title: Jeiel
jeiel.about: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeiel.note: One of the temple musicians when the ark came up. The name turns up often in Chronicles, for singers, scribes and officials.

jeremiah.title: Jeremiah
jeremiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeremiah.note: A priest's son from Anathoth, called as a young man in Josiah's thirteenth year. For four decades he told Judah Babylon was coming, and for that he was jailed, dropped in a cistern, and had his scroll burned. He saw Jerusalem fall as he had said, then was dragged off to Egypt against his will. His scribe Baruch may be the Berekhyahu on a clay seal from his lifetime.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jermoth-6.title: Jermoth
jermoth-6.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
jermoth-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

jermoth-7.title: Jermoth
jermoth-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jermoth-7.note: A common name among Levitical families and men after the exile. This one appears once.

jeroboam.title: Jeroboam
jeroboam.about: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy
jeroboam.note: Solomon's official who led the ten northern tribes out after Rehoboam refused to lighten the labour his father had laid on them. To stop his people going back to Jerusalem to worship, he set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan with a priesthood of his own. Every northern king after him gets measured against that sin.

jeroham-7.title: Jeroham
jeroham-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeroham-7.note: One of 7 men called Jeroham. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

jeruel.title: Jeruel
jeruel.note: Wilderness on the climb from the Dead Sea up toward Jerusalem, near Tekoa. Jehoshaphat's army met a coalition of Moabites, Ammonites and Meunites there and never had to fight, because God turned the invaders on each other.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jerusha.title: Jerusha
jerusha.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jerusha.note: She was Zadok's daughter, wife of King Uzziah and mother of Jotham, who reigned after him, and nothing more is recorded of her.

jeshanah.title: Jeshanah
jeshanah.note: Abijah of Judah captured this northern town from Jeroboam, with Bethel and Ephron, in a battle Judah won though badly outnumbered. It is generally identified with Burj el-Isaneh, north of Bethel. Nehemiah's Jeshanah gate in Jerusalem is a different thing.

jeshua-4.title: Jeshua
jeshua-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeshua-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jezreel.title: Jezreel
jezreel.note: A valley and town in northern Israel. Naboth's vineyard was there, the one Ahab and Jezebel stole, and it was there that Jehu wiped out Ahab's whole house. Hosea named one of his children Jezreel to say judgment was coming.

joah-4.title: Joah
joah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joah-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

joah-5.title: Joah
joah-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joah-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

joash.title: Joash
joash.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joash.note: Seven years old when he was made king of Judah, after six years hidden in the temple from his grandmother Athaliah, who had killed the rest of the royal family. While Jehoiada the priest lived, Joash ruled well and repaired the temple. Afterwards he let it go, and when Jehoiada's son stood up to him he had the man stoned in the temple court. His own murder followed.

joash-2.title: Joash
joash-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joash-2.note: A king of the north, and not the boy king of Judah who shares his name. He went down to weep over a dying prophet, and later he beat the king of Judah in battle when that king picked a fight with him.

joash-4.title: Joash
joash-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joash-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice across 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

joel-12.title: Joel
joel-12.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joel-12.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

jonathan.title: Jonathan
jonathan.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan.note: Saul's eldest son, heir to the throne, and David's friend. He made a covenant with David knowing it cost him the crown. Once, with only his armour-bearer, he climbed a cliff and started a rout of the Philistine army. He died with Saul and two brothers on Mount Gilboa, and David's lament for him says his love was "surpassing the love of women."

joram.title: Joram
joram.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joram.note: Another form of Jehoram, and the kings of Israel and Judah called by it are covered under that entry.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

josabad-3.title: Josabad
josabad-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
josabad-3.note: One of 9 men called Josabad. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

josabad-4.title: Josabad
josabad-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
josabad-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

josiah.title: Josiah
josiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
josiah.note: Made king of Judah at eight after his father Amon was murdered. In his eighteenth year workmen repairing the temple found a forgotten scroll of the law, and its reading set off Judah's last great reform: pagan altars torn down, the priests of the high places killed, and a Passover like none since the judges. He died young at Megiddo, trying to stop the Egyptian army reaching Assyria.

jotham.title: Jotham
jotham.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jotham.note: He carried on his father Uzziah's steady rule in Judah, building up Jerusalem's defences and bringing the Ammonites under, and Scripture counts him one of the few kings who did right in the Lord's eyes. The high places stayed, though.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kidron.title: Kidron
kidron.note: The valley along Jerusalem's east side, between the city and the Mount of Olives. Reforming kings dumped smashed idols and temple rubbish into it, and Jesus crossed it with his disciples on the way to Gethsemane the night he was arrested.

kirjath.title: Kirjath
kirjath.note: Kirjath-jearim, also called Baalah, a Gibeonite town on the line between Judah and Benjamin. The ark sat there twenty years after the Philistines gave it back, until David brought it up to Jerusalem. The prophet Uriah, whom Jehoiakim had killed, came from there.

kish-3.title: Kish
kish-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
kish-3.note: One of 4 men called Kish. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

kohathites.title: Kohathites
kohathites.about: Levi's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
kohathites.note: One of the three Levitical divisions, descended from Kohath. They carried the holiest furnishings, the ark among them, on poles and not in a cart, and 2 Samuel 6 shows what happened when that rule was broken. They camped south of the tabernacle. Moses, Aaron and Samuel were all Kohathites.

kore-2.title: Kore
kore-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
kore-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

lachish.title: Lachish
lachish.note: A heavily fortified Canaanite royal city in Judah's lowlands. Joshua took it, Rehoboam rebuilt it into one of Judah's strongest fortresses, and in 701 BC Sennacherib's Assyrians took it again. Assyria carved the siege on wall reliefs now in the British Museum. The ruins at Tell ed-Duweir also gave up the Lachish Letters, written during Babylon's last siege, just before Jerusalem fell.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

libnah.title: Libnah
libnah.note: A royal Canaanite city near Lachish that Joshua took and gave to the Levites in Judah. It held out against Sennacherib's Assyrians. Hamutal, Josiah's wife and mother of two of Judah's last kings, came from there.

maachah.title: Maachah
maachah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
maachah.note: Absalom's granddaughter, married to Rehoboam, and queen mother after him. Her grandson Asa took the title away because she promoted idol worship.

maaseiah-4.title: Maaseiah
maaseiah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
maaseiah-4.note: One of 20 men called Maaseiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

maaseiah-5.title: Maaseiah
maaseiah-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
maaseiah-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

maaseiah-6.title: Maaseiah
maaseiah-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
maaseiah-6.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

maaseiah-7.title: Maaseiah
maaseiah-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
maaseiah-7.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

mahalath-2.title: Mahalath
mahalath-2.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mahalath-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a woman from the divided-kingdom years.

mahath.title: Mahath
mahath.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mahath.note: A Kohathite Levite, named among the men who worked on cleaning out the temple.

mahath-2.title: Mahath
mahath-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mahath-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

manasseh-2.title: Manasseh
manasseh-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
manasseh-2.note: Hezekiah's son, who reigned in Judah longer than any king and did more harm than any. He rebuilt the high places, practiced sorcery, apparently sacrificed his own son, and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. Chronicles says captivity in Babylon broke his pride and he repented, but his reforms died with him.

mareshah.title: Mareshah
mareshah.note: Rehoboam fortified this Shephelah city, and Asa beat Zerah the Cushite's far larger army there. Micah mourns it among Judah's towns. Its ruins at Tell Sandahanna hold a Hellenistic underground city and painted Sidonian tombs full of exotic animals.

mattan.title: Mattan
mattan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mattan.note: A priest of Baal, killed at his own altar when the people of Jerusalem tore Baal's worship down after Queen Athaliah was overthrown.

mattaniah-4.title: Mattaniah
mattaniah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mattaniah-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

mattaniah-5.title: Mattaniah
mattaniah-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mattaniah-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

megiddo.title: Megiddo
megiddo.note: It guarded the pass into the Jezreel Valley. A Canaanite royal city, it went to Manasseh and Solomon rebuilt it as a chariot city. Deborah and Barak beat Sisera on its plain, and King Josiah died there facing Pharaoh Necho, a death mourned so deeply it became proverbial. Thutmose III's siege of it around 1457 BC is carved in detail on the walls of Karnak.

merari.title: Merari
merari.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
merari.note: Levi's third son. His descendants had the heavy parts of the tabernacle, the frames, bars, pillars and bases, which went by cart instead of being carried.

meshillemoth.title: Meshillemoth
meshillemoth.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
meshillemoth.note: Two men. The first was the father of Berechiah, an Ephraimite chief who stood against making slaves of Judean captives and had them fed, clothed and sent home. The second comes in the family line of Amashsai, a priest who settled in Jerusalem after the exile.

meshullam-9.title: Meshullam
meshullam-9.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
meshullam-9.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

micah.title: Micah
micah.note: In Judges, an Israelite who set up his own shrine with an idol and hired a wandering Levite as his private priest. Most of his verses belong to that story.

micaiah.title: Micaiah
micaiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
micaiah.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

michael-9.title: Michael
michael-9.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
michael-9.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

michaiah-2.title: Michaiah
michaiah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
michaiah-2.note: One of the officials Jehoshaphat sent round Judah to teach the law.

michaiah.title: Michaiah
michaiah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
michaiah.note: Mother of King Abijah of Judah, probably the woman called Maacah elsewhere.

miniamin.title: Miniamin
miniamin.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
miniamin.note: A priestly name of the years after the exile, carried by men who served in the temple and joined the dedication of the rebuilt walls.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moriah.title: Moriah
moriah.note: Abraham was told to take Isaac to the land of Moriah and offer him there. Chronicles puts Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. Jewish tradition has long taken the two as the same ridge.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

naamah.title: Naamah
naamah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
naamah.note: An Ammonite, one of Solomon's foreign wives, and the mother of Rehoboam, the only one of Solomon's wives named as a king's mother.

nahath-2.title: Nahath
nahath-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nahath-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nathan.title: Nathan
nathan.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan.note: The prophet who told David the story of the rich man who took a poor man's only lamb, let David condemn the man, and then turned it on him over Bathsheba and Uriah. Earlier he had brought God's promise that David's house would last forever. When David was dying, Nathan helped put Solomon on the throne ahead of a rival half-brother.

nebat.title: Nebat
nebat.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
nebat.note: Jeroboam's father, and he is only ever named in "Jeroboam son of Nebat," the phrase the books of Kings use again and again for the king blamed for making idol worship the habit of the north.

nebuchadnezzar.title: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nebuchadnezzar.note: King of Babylon. He destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC and carried Judah off, and the Bible still calls him the tool God used to judge his people. Daniel tells how, after boasting of his greatness, he went mad and lived like an animal for seven years, until he gave God the glory and got his throne back.

necho.title: Necho
necho.about: Pharaoh living at the time of Divided Monarchy
necho.note: Necho the Second, pharaoh of Egypt, killed King Josiah at Megiddo. Afterwards he removed Josiah's son Jehoahaz and set up another son, Jehoiakim, under him.

nethaneel-6.title: Nethaneel
nethaneel-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nethaneel-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

nethaneel-7.title: Nethaneel
nethaneel-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nethaneel-7.note: One of 10 men called Nethaneel. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

nethaniah-3.title: Nethaniah
nethaniah-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nethaniah-3.note: One of 4 men called Nethaniah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

nimshi.title: Nimshi
nimshi.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nimshi.note: Jehu's grandfather, who survives almost entirely inside the phrase "Jehu son of Nimshi."

obadiah-10.title: Obadiah
obadiah-10.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
obadiah-10.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

obadiah-9.title: Obadiah
obadiah-9.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
obadiah-9.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

obed-5.title: Obed
obed-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
obed-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

obed-edom.title: Obed-edom
obed-edom.about: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
obed-edom.note: After Uzzah died, David would not take the ark any further and left it in Obed-edom's house for three months. It brought blessing on his whole household, and that was what got David moving again.

oded.title: Oded
oded.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
oded.note: His son Azariah was the prophet who encouraged King Asa's reforms. Oded himself is only ever a father's name in 2 Chronicles 15.

oded-2.title: Oded
oded-2.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
oded-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a prophet from the divided-kingdom years.

omri.title: Omri
omri.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
omri.note: An army commander who took the northern throne after a civil war. He founded a dynasty. Assyrian records went on calling Israel the House of Omri long after he was dead.

ophel.title: Ophel
ophel.note: Temple servants lived on the Ophel, the fortified stretch of Jerusalem between the temple mount and the city of David, while Nehemiah was rebuilding the wall.

ophir.title: Ophir
ophir.note: It was the gold that made Ophir famous across the ancient world. Solomon's ships, sailing with Hiram of Tyre, brought it back in quantity, and the place itself was likely in southern Arabia or along the Red Sea.

ornan.title: Ornan
ornan.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ornan.note: The Jebusite who owned the threshing floor David bought to build an altar and stop the plague, the ground where Solomon's temple later stood. Ornan offered it for nothing, and David insisted on paying. He is also called Araunah.

parvaim.title: Parvaim
parvaim.note: Solomon got gold from Parvaim to overlay the temple, and nobody is sure where that was. Guesses run from Arabia to India. Some think the word just means the east.

pekah.title: Pekah
pekah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
pekah.note: He took the northern throne by murdering the king before him. Then he joined Syria against Assyria, invaded Judah, and tried to force King Ahaz into the alliance.

perizzite.title: Perizzite
perizzite.note: They come almost every time in a list, paired with the Canaanites, as one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel arrived.

persia.title: Persia
persia.note: The empire that took Babylon under Cyrus. Unlike the empires before it, Persia let the exiled Jews go home and rebuild their temple, and Ezra keeps the decree.

pharaoh-3.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-3.note: Solomon married his daughter. Pharaoh is a title rather than a name, and the record never gives this one any other.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

ramoth-gilead.title: Ramoth-gilead
ramoth-gilead.note: A city of refuge in Gad's land east of the Jordan, and too useful for Israel and Aram to leave alone. Ahab died after being wounded there trying to take it back with Jehoshaphat.

rehoboam.title: Rehoboam
rehoboam.about: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy
rehoboam.note: Solomon's son, and he lost most of the kingdom in his first days on the throne. The northern tribes asked him to lighten the heavy labour his father had laid on them. He turned down the older advisers and threatened them with worse.

remaliah.title: Remaliah
remaliah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
remaliah.note: Pekah's father. Isaiah keeps calling Pekah "the son of Remaliah," and it is not meant kindly.

samaria.title: Samaria
samaria.note: Omri bought a hill from a man called Shemer and built a capital on it. Samaria took over from Tirzah as the seat of the northern kingdom. Ahab and the kings after him ruled from there.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

seir.title: Seir
seir.note: A rough range of mountains east of the Arabah. It runs from the bottom of the Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqabah. The Horites lived there first, and Esau's descendants pushed them out.

sennacherib.title: Sennacherib
sennacherib.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
sennacherib.note: He besieged Jerusalem in Hezekiah's reign and boasted in his own inscriptions that he shut Hezekiah up like a bird in a cage. He never claims he took the city.

shallum-5.title: Shallum
shallum-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shallum-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice across 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

shallum-8.title: Shallum
shallum-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shallum-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

shamariah-2.title: Shamariah
shamariah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shamariah-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

sheba.title: Sheba
sheba.note: The Queen of Sheba came a long way, probably from southern Arabia. She came to test Solomon with hard questions. She went home saying the reports she had heard did not tell the half of it.

shecaniah-4.title: Shecaniah
shecaniah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shecaniah-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

shechem.title: Shechem
shechem.note: Abram stopped here when he first came into the land, and Joseph's brothers were grazing the flocks near it when Joseph went looking for them. The city took its name from a Canaanite prince.

shelomith-5.title: Shelomith
shelomith-5.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shelomith-5.note: A woman from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

shemaiah-13.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah-13.about: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemaiah-13.note: A levite from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

shemaiah-12.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah-12.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemaiah-12.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

shemaiah-14.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah-14.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemaiah-14.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

shemaiah-15.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah-15.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemaiah-15.note: One of 26 men called Shemaiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

shemaiah.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
shemaiah.note: The prophet who stopped Rehoboam from going to war with the northern tribes after the split. He said the division was God's own doing.

shemiramoth-2.title: Shemiramoth
shemiramoth-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemiramoth-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

shephatiah-7.title: Shephatiah
shephatiah-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shephatiah-7.note: One of 9 men called Shephatiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

shilhi.title: Shilhi
shilhi.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shilhi.note: His daughter Azubah married King Asa and was the mother of King Jehoshaphat, and that is why he is named.

shilonite.title: Shilonite
shilonite.note: A man from Shiloh. It is what they called the prophet Ahijah, who tore his cloak into twelve pieces to show that God would split Solomon's kingdom.

shimath.title: Shimath
shimath.note: An Ammonite woman. Her son Jehozabad and another man killed King Joash of Judah in his bed, reportedly in revenge for the prophet Zechariah.

shimeah-14.title: Shimeah
shimeah-14.about: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shimeah-14.note: A levite from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

shimeah-7.title: Shimeah
shimeah-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shimeah-7.note: 2 Chronicles names him twice, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

shimri-4.title: Shimri
shimri-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shimri-4.note: A common name among David's warriors and the families Chronicles lists. This one gets a single verse.

shimrith.title: Shimrith
shimrith.about: Moabite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shimrith.note: A Moabite woman whose son Jehozabad joined the plot that killed King Joash, in revenge for the prophet Zechariah (2 Chronicles 24:26).

shishak.title: Shishak
shishak.about: Pharaoh living at the time of United Monarchy
shishak.note: The pharaoh who invaded Judah in Rehoboam's reign and stripped Solomon's temple of its treasures. He put the campaign on a relief at Karnak, listing the towns.

shocho.title: Shocho
shocho.note: A town of Judah near the Valley of Elah, close to where David fought Goliath.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

succoth.title: Succoth
succoth.note: Jacob built shelters for his cattle here, east of the Jordan near the Jabbok, on his way back from Paddan-aram. The name means booths.

sukkiims.title: Sukkiims
sukkiims.note: They marched with Shishak's Egyptian army when it invaded Judah in Rehoboam's fifth year, alongside Libyans and Cushites. The name likely means tent-dwellers.

syrian.title: Syrian
syrian.note: The Arameans, the people around Damascus, mostly in the wars of the kings in 2 Kings.

tadmor.title: Tadmor
tadmor.note: It was Solomon's city out in the desert northeast of Damascus, on the caravan routes, and the Greeks and Romans knew it as Palmyra.

tarshish.title: Tarshish
tarshish.note: Far to the west, at the edge of what Israel knew of the sea. Solomon's ships went there for gold, and ships of Tarshish came to mean any big ocean-going ship. Jonah boarded one at Joppa to get away from Nineveh.

tekoa.title: Tekoa
tekoa.note: It sat about six miles south of Bethlehem, on the edge of the wilderness that carries its name. Rehoboam fortified it, and Amos was a herdsman there when he was called to prophesy against Israel.

tiglath-pileser.title: Tiglath-pileser
tiglath-pileser.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
tiglath-pileser.note: He was the third Assyrian king of the name, and he took territory from Israel and Syria and collected tribute. His own inscriptions record the same campaigns and payments 2 Kings describes.

timnah.title: Timnah
timnah.note: The Philistine town where Samson saw the woman he wanted to marry. The riddle at that wedding feast started his long fight with the Philistines.

tob-adonijah.title: Tob-adonijah
tob-adonijah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
tob-adonijah.note: A Levite Jehoshaphat sent around the cities of Judah with priests and other Levites, teaching from the Book of the Law.

tobiah.title: Tobiah
tobiah.about: Nehemiah's adversary living at the time of Exile and Return
tobiah.note: They called him the Ammonite. With Sanballat he mocked Nehemiah's wall and worked against it, and later a priest gave him a room inside the temple courts, so Nehemiah threw him and his things out.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

uri.title: Uri
uri.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
uri.note: Bezalel's father. Bezalel was the craftsman God picked to build the tabernacle and its furnishings.

uriel-3.title: Uriel
uriel-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
uriel-3.note: One of 3 men called Uriel. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Chronicles.

uzziah.title: Uzziah
uzziah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
uzziah.note: King of Judah at sixteen, he reigned fifty-two years and rebuilt the army and the economy. Then he went into the temple to burn incense himself, which no king was allowed to do. The priests confronted him and leprosy broke out on his forehead while he stood there.

uzziel-5.title: Uzziel
uzziel-5.about: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
uzziel-5.note: A levite from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

zabad.title: Zabad
zabad.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zabad.note: Several men carry the name. These verses are a man in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 2, and one in 2 Chronicles 24:26.

zachariah-10.title: Zachariah
zachariah-10.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zachariah-10.note: One of 29 men called Zachariah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles. The verse is 2 Chronicles 20:14.

zachariah-11.title: Zachariah
